column1: # Constructors and destructors bound to their original addresses for the port's link
# (tools/port_link.py --bindings; this file by default).
# A constructor or destructor keeps its C++ name in the sources: Clang 9 ignores an asm("fn_<addr>")
# label on one, and the port's host compiler hangs on it. tools/port_addresses.py places most of them
# from the byte-matching code that calls them. This table places the ones it cannot: no matched
# caller yet, or callers that disagree. tools/port_link.py treats each row like a placed address: a
# reference becomes an alias of the definition at that address (a matched fn_<addr>, else its lift),
# or a trap carrying the address.
# Columns, tab-separated: the mangled symbol, the address, what it is. A row that
# tools/port_addresses.py already places at the same address is redundant and says so in the link's
# output; one it places elsewhere is reported and left out (the matched code wins).
# Only one class per mangled name belongs here. A placeholder name that stands for different classes
# in different files (two files' UnkElem80) is a naming problem in the sources, to fix there.
